description:
## Goal

Resolve every callable reference exactly once through the ordinary lexical/expansion traversal, then retain its typed local or FunctionId identity through quote, macro execution, unquote, expansion, capture analysis, guards, and lowering. Source identifiers and qualified names exist only before resolution and for diagnostics or macro-visible display.

## Correct model

A module Namespace cannot identify local bindings. Local lexical identity is the pair of one typed SyntaxContext and the source identifier. One staged lexical environment and one set of scope operations begin in the existing expansion traversal: before values exist they record typed binding/classification by that key, and lowering realizes the same local keys to the existing ValueId. This is one authority across stages, not two algorithms sharing a key type. Do not add a LocalBindingId registry, parallel environment, quote-only name set, scanner, or side table.

SyntaxContext is structural and immutable. A source body begins with its typed function/source owner. Each macro expansion extends its parent context with the exact macro FunctionId and structural syntax address of the invocation. Child addresses follow explicit AST edges and sequence positions, not scheduling order, allocation order, a global counter, heap address, display text, or source span alone. Equal reproduction yields the same context; repeated and nested invocations remain distinct. Canonical output renders the typed owner and structural path, never raw World allocation numbers.

Executable map construction is the existing ordered `%{}` AST entry list. A raw runtime MAP is recursively inert quoted value data: AST-shaped tuples stored inside its keys or values do not expand, bind, capture, allocate generated functions, or establish execution order. This syntax/data boundary removes the old recursive raw-map walk and decoder sequencing whose storage order could change from ignored diagnostic metadata. Ordered map AST entries use the same explicit sequence-position addressing as other syntax; do not add a map comparator, map-key identity, snapshot, content hash, or map-only scope workaround.

Quote bodies are visited by that same binding traversal in an explicit template stage; unquote switches to the enclosing active stage. Quote-introduced binders and references share the invocation context supplied through `__CALLER__`, represented before execution as a typed context parameter rather than a provisional concrete context. Unquote preserves the inserted caller context. Fresh dynamically constructed syntax acquires the insertion context exactly once. Existing branch, clause, block, pattern, and lambda scope rules decide visibility and rebinding; the context distinguishes concordant names owned by different syntax. No later substitution, restamping, or repair pass exists.

Callable classification retains its result, never the Namespace consulted to obtain it. A visible contextual local remains one LexicalKey. A known or forward-declared definition becomes Bound(FunctionId), whose portable meaning is the existing FunctionDenotation. If classification genuinely depends on an unavailable interface, the attempt waits on that exact fact and classifies once after movement. A definitively missing definition retains only the typed definition owner, validated source reference and arity needed for its diagnostic; it cannot borrow a caller local and no later stage repeats namespace lookup. Fresh unannotated syntax constructed by a macro is classified once at insertion. Preserve the ordinary rule that macro classification precedes local callable dispatch.

Keep the standard quoted AST shape. Typed classification and syntax ownership are compiler-minted semantic metadata, distinct from visible metadata entries. Bound(FunctionId) and an already-classified Local(LexicalKey) are authoritative even if a macro changes the visible head spelling. A classified call visits its arguments but never rebuilds identity from that display head. Its display head is arbitrary quoted data: never expand, decode as source, or use it for dispatch. Copying classified metadata preserves its identity; constructing or editing visible integer and string fields cannot forge or retarget it. Argument changes validate bound arity and never choose another overload by spelling. Missing and fresh source references are validated at their one classification boundary, so guard and lowering paths never rely on unreachable shape assumptions.

World remains the one lookup authority. Macro-call expansion constructs Expansion(parent context, exact macro FunctionId, structural invocation address) before execution and projects it through the existing __CALLER__ value. Quote lowering reads dynamic invocation context through ordinary value steps.

Compiler-classified metadata is an intrinsic immutable annotation owned by the quoted metadata map, distinct from its visible entries. Its closed semantic encoding contains SourceDenotation, FunctionDenotation and the one recursive structural SyntaxContext. Compiler-only leaves may pair an exact SourceOwner or FunctionId as a transport coordinate. QuotedSourceHeap carries one World-domain token; decode checks that domain and verifies every coordinate against the semantic denotation already owned by World. It never resolves a name.

The optional annotation is inline heap-owned bytes on the map, not a resource, pointer, registry or side table. Ordinary fresh maps have no annotation. Copy, map derivation, deep copy and GC preserve it; visible metadata edits cannot forge or retarget it. Runtime equality and ordering compare the semantic encoding, never coordinates, allocation IDs or addresses. Canonical and AOT forms emit the semantic encoding and omit or relocate compiler-local coordinates, so unrelated allocation changes no artifact and quoting a cold callable demands no code.

Executable scope parity is mandatory: clause, branch, cond, with, lambda, and pin handling reuse the existing lowering visibility rules. Bitstring size expressions read locals and never introduce binders. Macro arguments preserve caller syntax ownership, but their final binding/reference role is determined at insertion; merely passing an argument does not execute syntax, bind locals, record captures, or allocate generated functions. Only executed unquote and context-parameter holes participate in enclosing executable captures.

Structural addresses include the owning module path in the source tree, the source-item position, grouped function-clause position, and every intervening AST edge. Restarting a scope or entering a demanded module cannot reset away an enclosing structural address.

The quoted read boundary decodes one exclusive typed metadata classification. It validates ordinary calls, bare function references, explicit arity, supported unresolved heads, and resolved module aliases without consulting Bound display data. A Bound target still observes callable kind and interface readiness; retaining identity does not bypass macro-before-local classification or dependency observation. An earlier accepted same-module declaration is classified from the existing FunctionSourceStash and callable-kind authority; a genuinely unknown external callable waits on its exact ModuleInterface. Once a FunctionId is selected, PlanEntryDispatch reads its local FunctionDefined plus its exact TypeDefined and StructDefined prerequisites. It publishes an entry plan whose helper calls retain only FunctionId and argument expressions; it does not consume child GuardDispatch values. ReifyGuardDispatch likewise publishes only its own function plan and body, without scanning or waiting through a transitive helper cone. Rooted backend packaging follows those exact typed edges during its existing graph walk, reads each settled GuardDispatch once, retains the shared World Arc, and rejects unsupported helper cycles in that same walk before native inlining. Neither entry planning nor downstream exact-body keying waits on the owning ModuleDefined aggregate, whose value it does not consume; each asks for its exact function, type, struct, guard or lowered-body fact, and the existing producer chain still materializes genuinely cold runtime modules. Delete the blanket dependency instead of publishing a provisional module or inventing a readiness fact. A definitively Missing target retains only its typed definition owner, validated source reference and arity for diagnostics. It retains no Namespace; a genuinely unavailable interface blocks before classification, and no later stage repeats lookup.

Identity publication binds the heap domain atomically with typed metadata construction. The macro execution boundary accepts owner-bearing quoted roots for the carrier, caller and every argument; all belong to the same execution heap and World domain before raw values enter runtime. A returned reference is therefore already owned by that heap. Bare AnyValueRef arguments, foreign-pointer retention, post-return rehoming and an implicit cross-heap importer are forbidden. Cross-heap semantic comparison validates the domain, semantic equality distinguishes foreign domains, and canonical lowering retains typed identities instead of erasing them to undistinguished integer constants. Exact SourceVersion provenance remains independent of syntax ownership throughout.

## TDD signal

Use the cross-source macro case exposed during fz-tfn.53: App binds FutureMacros only as F, requires F.twice/1, and the provider macro quotes a call to its own double/1 helper. Prove both separate submission orders, driving only after the provider exists: each returns 42 and lowers the helper to the exact provider FunctionId. fz-tfn.46 owns the earlier requester-drive boundary, where today's unknown-import failure must become an observed exact ModuleInterface dependency and resume only when that provider arrives.

Also prove a Provider module whose earlier helper/1 and make_answer/0 macro are followed by an item invocation of make_answer. The macro-generated answer/0 calls Provider.helper/1 and returns 42. EntryDispatch(make_answer) settles while ModuleDefined(Provider) is absent, records only its exact local function/type/struct reads, and changing an unrelated module causes no recomputation. Withholding each real type or struct prerequisite blocks entry planning exactly; withholding a referenced GuardDispatch blocks rooted backend packaging on that exact fact. Missing or private external callables remain rejected at the interface boundary.

Prove all lexical ownership cases:

- A provider literal helper(41) ignores a same-spelled caller-local closure.
- A quote-introduced local = unquote(cb); local(41) selects that exact local.
- In the same expansion, unquote(caller_call) retains the caller's same-spelled local rather than the quote-local binding.
- A quote-local binding does not leak into the caller expression that follows the expansion.
- Repeated and nested invocations of the same macro cannot capture one another's locals.
- Generated lambdas capture exact contextual locals.
- Existing macro-before-local classification is unchanged.
- Missing provider names retain their exact definition owner and diagnose there rather than borrowing caller locals.
- Fresh metadata resolves in its insertion context; copied metadata preserves ownership.

Prove that AST-shaped calls, bindings, and lambdas inside raw MAP data remain inert while repeated/nested calls in ordered `%{}` AST entries receive distinct contexts; reversing ignored raw-map metadata must mint no invocation or generated-function identity. Also prove copied metadata and head-only edits preserve a bound target or exact local key; argument edits cannot retarget overloads; malformed fresh or failed source references diagnose at classification; malformed and foreign-World typed metadata diagnose without panic; foreign macro callers or arguments are rejected before execution and cannot be laundered through an identity macro; arbitrary Bound display heads remain inert; and typed targets survive interpreter/native tuple-map transport. Assert typed lowered targets/captures, not rendered names. Preserve macro inspection/composition, semantic equality, deterministic unchanged/unrelated zero work, and byte-identical artifacts across allocation noise.

## Typed operator and guard cutover

Arithmetic and comparison syntax is classified by the ordinary expansion traversal and retains Bound(FunctionId). Kernel operators, imported operators and user-defined operators follow their exact selected definition; display heads and operator spelling are never semantic authority. True structural and control syntax, including pipe, cons and lazy and/or, remains syntax.

fz-5xp.30 supplies one typed Intrinsic identity for terminal compiler/runtime operations. GuardDispatch consumes the already-retained EntryDispatch plan for its function, preserving ordered clauses, typed parameter preconditions, outcomes, bindings and prepared keys. It owns only pure outcome bodies. A nested helper retains an exact FunctionId dependency edge to shared GuardDispatch; it never recursively clones another dispatch plan. Terminal work retains typed Intrinsic identity.

Guard evaluation is Value or Miss. Intrinsic fault, helper no-match and unsupported operands take the current ordered arms miss edge; they never become a false intermediate value or compiler-attempt failure. Lazy boolean control does not evaluate an untaken operand. This policy is shared by function, case and receive guards while each execution door retains only target-specific mechanics.

Delete direct_operator_name, source-name operator re-resolution, arithmetic/comparison PatternGuardBinOp reconstruction, guard clause-row reconstruction, boxed nested dispatch copies and the independent interpreter, entry-native and receive-native guard arithmetic/comparison authorities. Reuse FunctionId, EntryDispatch, GuardDispatch, LoweredBody and World fact edges; add no operator registry, purity store, guard scanner, solver or compatibility path.

## Dependency order

1. Pin contextual references, exclusive metadata validation, structural addresses, and domain transport.
2. Finish staged expansion scope and capture rules against existing lowering behavior.
3. Replace quote reconstruction with generic serialization and ordinary holes; delete restricted QuoteLowerer, quote-only name/operator reconstruction, and template traversal by ordinary executable diagnostics.
4. Cut ordinary calls, function references, guards, and captures onto the same typed targets. Preserve fz-tfn.64 outcome and guard ownership; only change the lexical-key seam.
5. Run the ownership/composition matrix, three-door transport, exact reuse, and allocation-noise canonical/artifact tests; update quoted-source and macro-expansion documentation.

## Strategy and deletion

Make the existing expansion traversal the one staged binding/classification authority while it walks syntax and classifies macros. It visits quote templates instead of skipping them, uses the same scope operations for ordinary and quoted syntax, and records contextual locals/captures and bound definition callables before macro execution. Serialize the already-classified quoted template generically, using ordinary lowering only for executed unquote and invocation-context holes. Delete the restricted QuoteLowerer reconstruction and its quote-only name/operator cases; ordinary executable diagnostics must not traverse template syntax. Generalize the existing lowering environment from String to the contextual lexical key and make it realize already-classified locals to ValueId; then delete downstream name-based local re-resolution and duplicate free-name authority. Collapse quote and ordinary call lowering onto the same typed target path.

Preserving full visible quoted shape must not add reactive work for dependency-free terminal locals: ABI and independently requested positioned TransportShape reuse the same pure layout calculator. Alias, container, callable, call-return and recursive positions retain their existing exact products.

Delete the blanket PlanEntryDispatch to owning ModuleDefined dependency. Delete quoted_callable_name and every canonical module.function string used as post-resolution authority. Delete serialized Namespace from classified callable metadata, downstream generated-call module-path re-resolution, and any workaround that adds provider names to caller namespaces or falls back from failed lexical lookup. Keep spelling and span only for fresh source classification, diagnostics, and macro-visible display.

Update quoted-source and macro-expansion documentation to state the single-resolution, syntax-context, and metadata contracts. Full focused/library/fixture/CLI gates, formatting, check, strict Clippy, deterministic reuse proof, and a fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review precede one commit and close. No temporary probe, duplicate traversal, compatibility path, or construction debris remains.
title: Keep callable identity through quoted source; delete canonical-name re-resolution
